Package com.egradx.audit.web

Class EgradxAuditExceptionHandler

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.core.web.EgradxExceptionHandlerSupport
com.egradx.audit.web.EgradxAuditExceptionHandler
@Order(-2147483648) @RestControllerAdvice(assignableTypes={EgradxAuditController.class,EgradxAuditPlatformController.class}) public class EgradxAuditExceptionHandler extends EgradxExceptionHandlerSupport
The audit endpoints' errors, in the envelope every EGRADX library answers with: everything they raise is a core exception or one of Spring's request errors, which EgradxExceptionHandlerSupport answers. Scoped to these two controllers, so it never answers for the host application's own.

Ordered first, as egradx-auth's is. Otherwise a host application's unscoped advice handling the same exception types wins or loses by registration order, and when it wins these endpoints answer in the application's envelope with its codes.
